analyst_view.overall: Liverpool (4th, 18 points) host Manchester United (18th, 8 points, their worst Premier League start) in the derby, and it is Mauricio Pochettino's first game after replacing Michael Carrick; he arrived from his US farewell midweek and has had at most three training sessions, so big tactical changes look unlikely so soon. Liverpool under Andoni Iraola have struggled at Anfield (four league goals in five home games, blanks against Arsenal, Manchester City and Fulham), but Iraola says van Dijk is fine, Gravenberch has trained for two days while managing pain and Frimpong should be available after five weeks out; Ekitike (counted), Bradley and Leoni are out. United are without Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte (all counted), Rashford is also out or doubtful with a hip problem but has barely played this season, and Luke Shaw is listed as injured by one preview and as a fitness check by another; Lisandro Martinez is back from his ban and Maguire and Dorgu have trained. The derby boost to cards (about +39%) and referee Sam Barrott (4.1 cards a game, close to average) are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already adding about 4% to Liverpool for United's leaky defence (16 conceded in six) and taking Sesko off United. Liverpool scored only four goals in their first five home league games this season and rank low for big chances created, and a new manager with three sessions usually starts by tightening up rather than opening the game, so I lean slightly lower: about 3.1. Rashford's absence changes little because he has hardly played.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, already trimming a little for Liverpool conceding few corners lately. United, in the bottom three, are likely to defend deeper at Anfield in Pochettino's first game, and Liverpool should have long spells pushing down the flanks, with Frimpong expected back in the squad; I lean mildly higher, about 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already adding about 39% for the derby, a little for Sam Barrott (4.1 a game in 54 games) and for United's high recent card count (16 in six). Mac Allister is one booking from a ban, and a United side defending deep may still commit tactical fouls, but the derby boost is already large, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already adding about 12% to United for their busy attacking under Carrick (96 shots in six). Away at Anfield, without their striker Sesko and with a new manager who has had little time on the training ground, United are likely to take fewer attempts than that, which outweighs Liverpool's near-full attack: about 30.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already adding about 7% to Liverpool for United conceding plenty on target lately. Fewer United attempts and Liverpool's weak home finishing this season pull down, while a mostly fit Liverpool attack with Isak and Wirtz, plus United's leaky defence, pull up, so I stay at 9.8.
